text:
Anne: FYI we hit a weird warmup hang on canary when serving gzipped safetensors. Warmup tasks spin on range reads; not full OOM but no forward progress.
sre-bot: [warmup-alert] shard=expr_v3_shard06 event=range_retry_spike
Jason: can you paste the minimal logs?
Anne: here \\u2014 notice the repeated 206 + checksum mismatch: 
```
2026-03-20T09:07:02Z fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
2026-03-20T09:07:02Z verify checksum post-decompress expected=deadbeef got=00000000
2026-03-20T09:07:02Z backoff sleep=40ms attempt=1
2026-03-20T09:07:03Z fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
```
Priya: sounds like we verify after decompressing (current loader behavior), but when the server responds with partial gz stream that splits header/CRC across ranges we decompress garbage and checksum fails.
Carlos: storage sometimes serves gzipped object; our streaming loader requested small ranges which can slice mid-gzip-header. Decompressor then sees invalid stream.
Jason: quick mitigation options: increase the initial priming range so the first fetch contains the entire gzip header+first blocks, or switch to verifying compressed payload bytes (if manifest carries a compressed checksum) before decompressing.
Anne: I prototyped upping initial range to 128k; canary shows fewer stalls but higher bytes transferred for small shards.
Priya: another idea: on checksum fail, instead of immediate fail, do an "elastic priming" flow: attempt a single larger read (e.g., 512k) and only fail if that larger read also mismatches. That reduces wasted bandwidth on large shards while addressing header-split cases.
Jason: agrees. Also API/ABI decision: should the loader return decompressed safetensors only, or should it surface raw compressed bytes and allow the runtime to decompress? I prefer loader to present decompressed data (consistency for downstream), but loader should be explicit about the compression metadata.
Carlos: implement manifest fields: `compression: "gzip"` and optional `compressed_sha256`. Loader behavior: if `compressed_sha256` present -> fetch first N bytes, verify compressed checksum, then decompress. If absent -> use elastic priming heuristic.
Priya: metrics to add: `loader.gz_header_mismatch`, `loader.gz_elastic_primes`, `loader.gz_compressed_verify_fail`. Tag with `shard`,`model`,`region`,`deployment_tier`.
Anne: test plan: (1) unit tests for partial-gzip streams (simulate server returning headers split across ranges), (2) integration with a local HTTP stub that supports range responses and can inject gz splits, (3) canary rollout with telemetry gating.
Jason: retry strategy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries for range reads; on repeated checksum failures escalate to elastic prime flow.
Carlos: storage doc updated: prefer serving uncompressed safetensors for hot shards, but when compression is used include compressed checksum in manifest. Also add a note for CDNs that may re-chunk objects.
Priya: long-term: per-chunk (subrange) checksums so we can validate each block independently and avoid large priming reads. That will need a new on-disk layout or sidecar index.
Anne: short-term action items: Priya -> manifest PR to add `compression` + `compressed_sha256` + schema bump. Jason -> loader PR: elastic priming + compressed-verify path + metrics. Carlos -> storage test harness and doc update. I'll open an RFC follow-up summarizing choices and add a rollout checklist.
Jason: I'll add the unit and integration tests to the PR and flag you for review, @Priya.
Priya: on it. I'll include example manifests and compatibility notes.
sre-bot: ticket INF-8741 created: "loader: gzip priming & compressed checksum support" assigned to eng-ml.
Anne: thanks folks, let's sync in next standup if canary shows regressions. :+1:
